concern: Enhanced cytotoxicity with reduced therapeutic index
system_prompt: You are a senior medicinal chemist specializing in prodrug design and ADMET optimization. Always respond with valid JSON containing a 'modifications' list. Each modification must include 'description', 'smiles', and 'rationale' fields.

modifications.description: Introduce a phosphate ester at the primary alcohol of the sugar moiety to enhance water solubility and enable activation by phosphatases in target tissues.
modifications.rationale: Phosphate esterification increases water solubility, improving bioavailability. Phosphatase enzymes overexpressed in tumor environments can cleave the phosphate group, releasing active doxorubicin selectively at the target site.

modifications.description: Attach a hydrophobic targeting moiety (e.g., folate group) via an ester linkage to the ketone group on the anthracycline ring to enhance tumor-specific uptake.
modifications.rationale: Folate receptors are overexpressed on many cancer cells. Attaching a folate group can facilitate receptor-mediated endocytosis, enhancing tumor-specific uptake and reducing systemic toxicity.

modifications.description: Incorporate a cleavable peptide linker to the ketone group on the anthracycline ring to allow activation by tumor-specific proteases.
modifications.rationale: Proteases such as matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) are upregulated in the tumor microenvironment. A cleavable peptide linker ensures selective release of doxorubicin in cancerous tissues, minimizing off-target effects.
